harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (a SONiC-VS box) as an L3 router forwarding between node2 and node3 over two point-to-point links (eth1/enp8s0=192.168.12.0/30, eth2/enp8s0=192.168.13.0/30), enabled IP forwarding, and added an nftables forward-hook ACL on node1 that explicitly accepts TCP/8080 and rejects (TCP RST) TCP/23 in both directions between node2 and node3, while leaving the default-accept forward policy untouched for all other traffic (verified with a control port 9999 and ICMP). All config was made persistent (ifupdown drop-in for link IPs, sysctl.d for forwarding, a systemd oneshot service to reapply the nft ACL table on boot; NetworkManager static profiles on node2/node3 for the link IPs and routes). Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id and health, rebooted, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified the ACL/data path after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 network state and identified the private link NICs (node1 eth1/eth2, node2/node3 enp8s0)
Assigned static point-to-point IPs: node1 eth1=192.168.12.1/30 <-> node2 enp8s0=192.168.12.2/30; node1 eth2=192.168.13.1/30 <-> node3 enp8s0=192.168.13.2/30
Discovered NetworkManager on RHEL10 nodes was reverting raw `ip addr add` changes; reconfigured via nmcli static profiles with persistent static routes to the peer subnet via node1
Enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding on node1
Opened local firewalld test ports (8080/23/9999) on node2/node3 to allow end-to-end validation of node1's forwarding policy
Captured a pre-ACL baseline proving 8080, 23, 9999, and ICMP all forward through node1 by default
Added nft table inet transit_acl on node1's forward hook: accept tcp/8080 and reject (tcp reset) tcp/23 between eth1/eth2 in both directions, leaving the accept-all base policy for all other traffic
Verified bidirectionally: 8080 succeeds, 23 is refused (connection refused/reset), and 9999 + ICMP remain unaffected

Persisted config for reboot survival: /etc/network/interfaces.d/transit-links (static link IPs), /etc/sysctl.d/99-transit-acl.conf (forwarding), /usr/local/sbin/transit-acl-apply.sh + transit-acl.service (re-applies the nft ACL table at boot without touching the docker-managed iptables-nft tables)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all three nodes

Restarted node1 via `systemctl reboot` (backgrounded so the ack returned first), polled until exec was available, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified forwarding IPs, nft ACL table, and live 8080/23/ICMP traffic
Restarted node2 the same way, confirmed boot_id changed, restored test firewall ports/listeners, and re-verified traffic
Restarted node3 the same way, confirmed boot_id changed, restored test firewall ports/listeners, and re-verified traffic
Ran a final full end-to-end check (8080 accept, 23 refused, ICMP unaffected) after all three nodes had been independently restarted

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other on TCP 8080 through node1
evidence.summary: Pre-ACL baseline and post-ACL tests show TCP/8080 connects and round-trips data in both directions (node2->node3 and node3->node2)

evidence.requirement: node1 refuses TCP 23 between node2 and node3
evidence.summary: socat connect attempts on port 23 in both directions return 'Connection refused' after the nft reject-with-tcp-reset rule was applied, versus succeeding in the pre-ACL baseline (cmd-f54c028fb30b42c1)

evidence.requirement: rest of forwarded traffic left untouched
evidence.summary: Control port 9999/TCP and ICMP continue to forward successfully through node1 after the ACL was applied, matching pre-ACL baseline behavior

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline health and boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id=39fdb9ab... plus healthy nft ACL table, forwarding sysctl, and link IPs before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect, node1 unreachable during reboot, then boot_id changed to f61cbe93... confirming an actual restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery proof
evidence.summary: After restart, forwarding sysctl, link IPs, and nft transit_acl table were all restored by the persistence units; live TCP/8080 accept, TCP/23 refuse, and ICMP traffic verified end-to-end through node1

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline health and boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured node2 boot_id=434803ac... and healthy link IP/route state before restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged before disconnect, node2 unreachable during reboot, then boot_id changed to e0ad1783... confirming restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: post-restart recovery proof
evidence.summary: Link IP/route auto-restored via NetworkManager persistent profile; live TCP/8080 accept and TCP/23 refuse verified from node3 to node2 after restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline health and boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured node3 boot_id=73237116... and healthy link IP/route state before restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged before disconnect, node3 unreachable during reboot, then boot_id changed to ca8f8f03... confirming restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: post-restart recovery proof and final cross-node verification
evidence.summary: Link IP/route restored on node3; final end-to-end test after all three nodes independently restarted shows TCP/8080 accept, TCP/23 refuse, and ICMP unaffected
